text:
Marathon Petroleum fell 1.55% today after oil prices retreated on October 15th, despite the day before's gains driven by Middle East supply worries. The retreat came as traders digested the International Energy Agency's latest report and reassessed the severity of ongoing Iranian attacks on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz—the initial shock and supply-disruption premium faded as the market found its footing. The stock had surged nearly 14% over the past two weeks as geopolitical tensions lifted crude prices and refinery economics improved.

Refineries are currently running at 92.7% capacity with crude prices still elevated—US oil at $96 a barrel—so the underlying business backdrop remains solid. The swings reflect how tightly Marathon's fortunes track both crude price movements and the real-time flow of news from conflict zones that could choke off global oil supply.
